set.n: The fish-worm pot: Capt. Suiter's cellar gold, Le Claire (1900)
set.v: $200-300 in gold coin and two silver pieces in an iron pot (recovered)
set.tovw: Lead grade F (treasure thread): found and recovered 1900
set.t: Recovered in 1900. The river-town saloon pattern is the only lead it offers. House lots: look only.
pinev: GNIS Le Claire (41.5986,-90.3435); the Suiter house (built c.1850, once a saloon) is not identified.

tw-ia-le-claire-suiter-cellar-1900.st: The Marshalltown paper adds that he was a river man formerly of the steamer Verne Swain, that the iron pot held $200-300 in gold and two silver pieces, and that the house had been a saloon when Le Claire 'was one of the toughest river towns along the Mississippi'; it supposed someone in trouble buried the pot and never came back.
src: Evening Times-Republican (Marshalltown), 1 Sep 1900, p. 3, 'Gold in His Cellar' (Newspapers.com 352079495)
